name: Athpariya

catalog_locator: p. 3, section 1.2.4 'Some typological features'; restated p. 79, section 9.1.1 item (g) and p. 7 digest of Eppele et al. 2012 'A non-tonal language'

tone_statements.citation: Regmi, Ambika. 2016. A sociolinguistic survey of Athpariya: a Tibeto-Burman language. Kathmandu: Linguistic Survey of Nepal (LinSuN), Central Department of Linguistics, Tribhuvan University. 131 pp.
tone_statements.quote: Ebert (1994; 1997) and Neupane (2058 B.S.) present a cluster of typological features in the domains of phonology, morphology and syntax in Athpariya. They are presented as follows: (a) Athpariya is a non-tonal language. It has five oral vowel and 25 consonant phonemes. Length is not contrastive.
tone_statements.locator: p. 3, sec. 1.2.4 'Some typological features' item (a) (repeated p. 7 sec. 1.5 'Previous research works')
tone_statements.summary: Sociolinguistic survey; states Athpariya is a non-tonal language (relaying Ebert 1994/1997 and Neupane 2001), with 5 vowels, 25 consonants, no contrastive length. Nothing on word stress.

sources.note: Nothing. The whole phonology chapter (1.1 Consonants, 1.2 Vowels, 1.3 Syllable structure and phonotactics: assimilation, voicing, insertion, deletion) contains no statement on stress, accent or tone; the only prosody-adjacent remark is p.15 'Vowels are somewhat lengthened in open root syllables. No minimal pairs based on vowel length were found.' Author's caveat p.13: 'Phonology is the part of grammar on which I have spent least time. I can therefore only give a rough sketch'.
